items.text: The British government has approved drilling at a controversial North Sea gas field, despite strong opposition from environmental groups. Energy companies welcomed the decision and predicted the project could supply over six percent of the nation’s gas at peak production. Officials argue that developing domestic resources is necessary to boost national energy security while global conflicts drive up fuel costs. The prime minister stated that although the country remains committed to long-term climate targets, oil and gas will still be needed during the transition to renewable energy. However, climate activists and politicians heavily criticized the approval and warned that increased fossil fuel reliance won’t lower household energy bills because prices are dictated by international markets. They stress that true security requires a faster shift toward clean energy rather than expanding fossil fuel infrastructure. Difficult words: controversial (causing a lot of angry public discussion and strong disagreement), dictate (to state, order, or control authoritatively how something must be done or decide), reliance (dependence on someone or something for help or support). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The UK government approved a new project to drill for gas in the North Sea. Energy companies say this project will help produce more gas for the country. Leaders argue that using local gas makes the country safer as global conflict causes energy prices to rise. The prime minister explained that the country still needs gas while moving toward green energy. Environmental groups and green politicians strongly disagree with the plan. They warn that drilling produces harmful emissions and will not lower electricity bills for normal families. Activists argue that the government should focus on renewable energy like wind and solar instead of fossil fuels. Difficult words: approve (to officially agree), harmful (when something hurts living things or the planet), renewable energy (energy from natural sources, such as wind, sun, and so on). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The UK government says yes to getting new gas from under the sea. There is a plan to drill in the North Sea. Leaders say that this gas will help keep the country safe when energy prices are high. The prime minister says that the country still needs gas, but it also wants clean energy in the future. Many people are very angry about this decision . They say that getting more gas is bad for the planet. It will not help people get cheaper electricity. They want the government to use clean power like wind and sun instead of oil and gas. Difficult words: drill (to make a hole in the earth to get oil or gas), price (how much money something costs), decision (what you do after thinking or talking about it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Salmon farming is a growing, multi-billion-dollar industry. The biggest producers, Norway and Chile, have seen booming profits; however, the industry is facing problems such as mass salmon die-offs, infectious diseases, and environmental damage. Fish farming relies heavily on chemicals and antibiotics to treat parasites that can weaken or kill the fish. A large farm in Norway, Norlock, uses freshwater baths and chemical treatments to combat salmon lice, but these methods can also stress the fish and lead to further health issues. One innovative solution at Norlock involves using laser technology to remove the parasites, reducing infection rates. Also, farms in open sea environments benefit from ocean currents, which can help wash away waste and reduce diseases. Chile’s salmon farms, which are heavily dependent on antibiotics, are also under scrutiny for their environmental impact. New methods like closed aquaculture systems, which keep farmed fish in tanks and prevent contamination, offer hope for a more sustainable future in salmon farming. Difficult words: parasite (an organism that lives in or on an organism and feeds from it), innovative (featuring new methods), scrutiny (critical and detailed examination). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Salmon farming is a big business and Norway and Chile are the leading producers of farmed salmon. The industry makes billions of dollars, but issues like diseases, fish deaths, and parasites are becoming hard to control. In Norway, farms like Norlock are trying to reduce the number of sick fish. They use chemicals, freshwater baths, and even lasers to kill parasites. But even with these new technologies, salmon farming has a lot of problems. Farmed salmon often escape from the nets and can spread disease to wild salmon. In Chile, salmon farms use large amounts of antibiotics to fight diseases, but this can also harm the environment and human health. Some salmon farms are trying new methods, like closed aquaculture, where they keep fish in tanks instead of in open water. This could help make salmon farming more sustainable in the future. Difficult words: parasite (an animal or plant which lives on another animal or plant and feeds from it), escape (to get free from a place), antibiotic (a medicine which destroys bacteria in the body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Salmon farming is a big business. But it has some problems. Norway and Chile are the biggest salmon producers. The fish often get sick or die. Small parasites attack the fish and make them weak . It is not easy to stop the parasites. Some farms, like Norlock in Norway, use chemicals, fresh water, and even lasers to kill them. In Chile, farms use a lot of medicine to keep the fish healthy. But this can hurt the environment . Some farms are now trying a new way of farming. They use big tanks instead of open water. This could help make salmon farming better for the environment. Difficult words: parasite (an animal or plant which lives on another and feeds from it), weak (not strong enough), environment (the natural world). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Popular beaches in eastern Sydney were closed to the public after a dead young humpback whale washed ashore in a rocky bay. Local authorities shut down swimming and surfing spots as a safety precaution and warned that the whale carcass is likely to attract sharks to the coastline. Emergency teams and local rangers face significant challenges trying to remove the body because the animal is in an advanced state of decomposition, and the rough ocean conditions make the area inaccessible for boats or heavy machinery. Community leaders and experts noted that with growing whale populations along the coast, such events are becoming more common. Indigenous rangers plan to perform cultural ceremonies to honor the whale, while scientists advise the public to stay out of the water and let nature take its course if retrieval remains impossible. Difficult words: precaution (an action taken in advance to prevent something dangerous, unpleasant, or inconvenient from happening), carcass (the dead body of an animal, especially a large one), retrieval (getting something back or removing it from a specific location). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Officials closed famous Australian beaches after a dead young whale washed up on rocky shores near Sydney. Lifeguards shut the beaches to keep swimmers safe because the whale carcass can attract dangerous sharks. Local teams are trying to figure out how to handle the situation, but removing the heavy animal is extremely difficult. The ocean is rough, and the body is already breaking down. Experts say that more whales are migrating along the coast this season, which makes these events more common . Indigenous groups are preparing special cultural ceremonies to respect the animal. For now, local leaders ask people to stay away from the water until the coast is clear and safe again. Difficult words: carcass (the dead body of an animal), migrate (to move from one region to another according to the seasons), common (happening often). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A dead whale washes up on the rocks near Sydney, Australia. Local leaders close nearby beaches to keep people safe. They are worried that the big dead animal will bring hungry sharks near the shore . Workers cannot easily move the whale. The water is dangerous, and the rocks are sharp. Also, the body is already breaking down into parts. Experts say that many whales are swimming near the land this month. Local people and rangers want to do a special ceremony for the animal. Leaders tell visitors not to swim in the sea right now. Difficult words: wash up (when water carries something onto the land), shore (the land along a sea or lake), break down (to separate into smaller parts over time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The urgent need to combat weeds sustainably has been heightened by global warming, which accelerates their growth, posing a threat to crops and food security. Traditional methods involve excessive chemical spraying, resulting in environmental harm. Startups like Precision AI are introducing innovative solutions, such as AI-enabled crop-spraying drones, which reduce chemical usage by up to 90%. These drones employ AI to precisely identify plant species in real-time, allowing targeted chemical applications to eliminate weeds while minimizing environmental impact. Currently, a significant portion of chemicals applied in agriculture goes to waste. Precision AI aims to shift the industry towards a ‘spray as a service’ model, leveraging precision farming technologies. Despite the potential benefits, challenges include navigating international regulations, scaling up the technology, and addressing concerns about job displacement due to autonomous farming. Difficult words: heighten (to make or become more intense), leverage (to use borrowed money for investments), scale up (to increase something in size, number, or extent). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Farmers need to deal with weeds in a more environmentally friendly way. Global warming makes weeds grow faster which means that farmers must use more chemicals. The surprising fact is that 95% of these chemicals go into the soil or they end up on plants. Spraying fields is expensive and very inefficient . Startups like Precision AI are introducing a fresh approach with AI-powered drones which reduce chemical use by up to 90%. Traditional farming uses expensive machines like ground sprayers, which cost a lot and farmers use them only a few weeks a year. Precision AI uses AI drones which scan fields, check plant types, and spray only the weeds. This saves about 95% of chemicals compared to old methods. Difficult words: weed (a wild plant which grows where people do not want it), approach (the way of dealing with a problem or situation), inefficient (a person, system, or machine that does not work in the best way and wastes money, time or energy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Weeds are wild plants. They grow in fields. Farmers do not want them in their fields. Farmers use a lot of chemicals . These chemicals kill weeds. But chemicals are not good for nature. Most farming machines are big and expensive. They work only a little bit every year. Another problem is that most chemicals end up in soil and on plants. This way of farming is expensive and it does not work very well. One company makes drones . These drones use AI. The drones fly over fields. They find weeds. They spray only weeds. This saves money and the planet, too. The drones save 95% of chemicals. Difficult words: chemical (a substance which does not come from nature), soil (the brown substance in which plants grow), drone (a small flying vehicle which a person operates). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New York City lawmakers will vote on a bill to ban Central Park’s historic horse-drawn carriages by June 2028. Activists have long argued that operating horses on busy city streets is inhumane and unsafe. Support for the ban surged following a fatal accident in which a young tourist died when a horse bolted . City officials, including the mayor, support the phase-out and propose transition plans to compensate owners and protect horses from being slaughtered. However, the proposal faces strong opposition from drivers and the Transport Workers Union, who argue that the tradition has existed since the 1800s and provides a livelihood for hundreds of workers. While some visitors regret losing an iconic city tradition, others welcome the change and point to modern alternatives that don’t involve animal labor. Difficult words: inhumane (causing unnecessary suffering to people or animals; without kindness), bolt (to suddenly run away out of control, usually because of fear or shock), phase-out (ending or stopping something gradually over a period of time). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

New York City is planning to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park by June 2028. Animal rights groups criticized the carriages for years and said the horses work in unsafe conditions alongside cars. Support for the ban grew stronger after a tourist died in an accident involving a carriage. While the city mayor supports the new law, drivers and union workers are fighting against it. They say the carriages are a famous tradition from the 1800s and that the ban will destroy many jobs. The city plans to help workers transition and promises that the horses will not be killed. While some tourists will miss the classic rides, many people believe it is time to stop using horses for entertainment . Difficult words: union (an official organization of workers formed to protect their rights and interests), transition (the process or period of changing from one state or job to another), entertainment (activities provided for people to enjoy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New York City wants to stop horse carriages in Central Park by 2028. Many people say that working in the city is bad and dangerous for horses. A bad accident with a horse happens some time ago. A tourist dies. Now, city leaders want to ban the rides. Drivers and workers are sad and angry. They will lose their jobs. They say that carriages are an old tradition . It belongs to New York since the 1800s. City leaders want to help the workers and keep the horses safe. Many visitors say that it is time to keep the animals safe. There are other ways to see the park than using horses. Difficult words: horse carriage (a vehicle with wheels which a horse or more horses pull), ban (an official stop), tradition (something what people do for a long time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Recent news reports reveal that Elon Musk personally authorized a slowdown of Starlink, the military-grade satellite network crucial to Ukraine’s defense against Russia. The restriction severely hampered Ukrainian military operations, affected drone capabilities and missile interceptions . While some US officials suggest Musk acted on his own, other sources indicate he discussed the decision with President Trump and administration members. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Starlink service remains limited, though American officials promised to help resolve the issue. The incident triggered strong outrage in Washington, and lawmakers call for a full investigation into potential contract violations and illegal interference. Commentators and politicians expressed deep concern over the dangerous concentration of geopolitical power in the hands of a single private citizen during wartime. Difficult words: hamper (to delay something or prevent it from progressing), interception (stopping or catching something before it reaches its destination), violation (breaking a rule, law, or agreement). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Reports show that Elon Musk ordered a slowdown of Starlink’s military internet service, which Ukraine relies on to defend itself from Russian attacks. The restriction made it much harder for Ukrainian forces to use drones and protect cities. While some leaders think Musk acted completely on his own, others say he spoke with President Trump before making the decision. Ukrainian President Zelensky said that connection speeds are still limited , but officials are working to fix the problem. The situation made many American politicians angry, and they are now demanding a full investigation. Many people believe that an ordinary person shouldn’t have the power to control military decisions or affect international war strategy. Difficult words: slowdown (reducing the speed or activity of something), restriction (a rule which controls what can be done), limited (not working fully). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new report says that Elon Musk slows down the satellite internet for Ukraine. It is called Starlink. Ukraine uses Starlink to fight against Russia. This makes it very hard for Ukrainian soldiers to use drones and stop rockets. Ukraine’s president says that the internet is still slow, but leaders are trying to fix it. Some people say that Musk talks to Donald Trump first. Others think that he does it alone . American politicians are very angry. They want to find out what really happens. They believe that one rich man should not have so much power in a war. Difficult words: fix (to make something work again), alone (without other people or help), power (when you can control or have an impact on what happens to other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Using the example of twin sisters Morgan and Lisa living in identical houses, we can explore the financial realities of buying versus renting a home over 30 years. Morgan bought her home for 400,000 dollars, paid a 50,000 down payment and closing costs, followed by fixed monthly mortgage payments, property taxes, maintenance, and repair expenses. Lisa opted to rent. She started at 1,800 dollars a month with significantly lower initial costs, and invested her unused down payment capital into a diversified retirement fund. Over three decades, Morgan spent 1.4 million dollars on housing and repairs, but her home grew in value to 1.3 million, which gave her long-term equity and lower future costs once the mortgage was paid off. On the other hand, Lisa spent 900,000 dollars in total rent, but her invested savings grew to 500,000. While Morgan achieved a better overall financial net position, Lisa enjoyed lower short-term expenses, freedom from maintenance responsibilities, and geographic flexibility. Difficult words: down payment (a cash payment made when buying a house or expensive item, covering a part of the total price), initial (happening at the beginning of a process or event), equity (the financial value of a property minus the remaining mortgage debt owed on it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

To see if buying or renting a home is better, we can follow twin sisters Morgan and Lisa over 30 years. Morgan bought a house for 400,000 dollars and she used a mortgage loan . She had to pay a large down payment and all repair costs herself. She spent 1.4 million in total, but her house became worth 1.3 million. On the other hand, Lisa rented her house, which means she started with much smaller costs. Her landlord paid for all home repairs, and Lisa invested her saved cash into a retirement account. After 30 years, Lisa spent 900,000 dollars on rent, but her investments grew to 500,000. While buying gave Morgan a stronger financial outcome in the long run, renting provided Lisa with more freedom, flexibility to move, and lower monthly costs early on. Difficult words: mortgage loan (a bank loan for buying a house), down payment (the money which you pay at the beginning when you buy a house), landlord (a person or company which owns a house or flat and rents it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Twin sisters Morgan and Lisa move into the same kind of house. Morgan buys her home. Lisa rents hers. Morgan must pay a lot of money in the beginning. She repairs the house when things break. After 30 years, Morgan pays off her home loan, and her house becomes worth a lot of money. She buys the house for 400,000 dollars. After 30 years, she can sell it for 1.3 million. Lisa pays rent every month. She does not pay for repairs. She saves money. She has a retirement account . After 30 years, she pays 900,000 dollars for rent. But she has 500,000 in her retirement account. In the end, Morgan makes more money by buying. But Lisa is free to move. She can spend on hobbies, not a house. Difficult words: twin sister (a girl who is born at the same time to the same mother as another child), rent (the money which you pay when you live in someone’s house or flat), retirement account (an account where you save money for the time after finishing work). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Independent Australian lawmaker Helen Haines remains in critical condition following a shocking vehicle attack outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria. A 43-year-old suspect allegedly rammed his car into her while she was standing near the trunk of her vehicle, and then backed up to strike her again. A local barber disarmed and held the suspect until police arrived. Authorities have charged the suspect, while counterterrorism units and federal police assist with the investigation. The attack resulted in the amputation of one of the woman’s legs, and surgeons are working to save her other leg. Haines is known for her political integrity and independent work representing regional interests, and she is widely respected across party lines. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called the event a deliberate act and warned against growing hostility and rhetoric directed at elected officials. The incident has raised deep concerns about security and the changing safety of public access to politicians in Australia. Difficult words: electorate office (an office maintained by an elected representative in their local district to serve and meet with local citizens), amputation (the surgical removal of a limb or part of the body), hostility (aggressive, unfriendly behavior or feelings towards someone), rhetoric (language used to influence people, often used in political debates). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

An Australian politician named Helen Haines is fighting for her life after a driver deliberately hit her with a car outside her office. She suffered severe injuries, and doctors had to amputate her leg. A brave local barber stopped the driver and took away a knife he had before police arrested him. Police charged a 43-year-old man in connection with the attack. Australian Prime Minister condemned the attack and asked leaders to stop angry political language across the country. People know Haines as a popular politician who works closely with her local community. This terrible event shocked Australians and raised serious worries about safety for politicians who normally meet people easily in public. Difficult words: deliberately (done on purpose), amputate (to cut off a part of the body), condemn (to openly say that you disagree with something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

An Australian politician named Helen Haines is badly hurt. A man in a car attacks her outside her office. She loses a leg in the hospital. The driver hits her on purpose . A local barber helps stop the driver. Police catch him. He is 43 years old. Australian leaders are very sad and shocked . Haines is a kind person who works hard for her area. Australian Prime Minister asks people to stop using bad and angry words in politics. Many people wish Haines to get well soon. Difficult words: on purpose (when you do something and you plan it before), barber (a person who cuts and styles people’s hair and men’s beards), shocked (very surprised and upset). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

As Israel approaches its national election, security strategy toward Iran has become a central campaign issue. Public opinion polls show that a majority of Israeli voters oppose stopping military attacks on Iran. This leaves Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu open to criticism from opposition rivals who argue he failed to achieve total victory. The lead opposition candidate contends the conflict remains unfinished and highlights that Tehran keeps hundreds of kilograms of highly enriched uranium capable of producing multiple nuclear weapons. Other opposition figures support aggressive military action, including targeting Iranian energy infrastructure to collapse the regime’s economy. While the opposition shares the goal of confronting regional adversaries and expanding diplomatic alliances, critics warn that their proposed policies rely heavily on continuous military dominance. Meanwhile, opposition leaders express concern that Netanyahu might intentionally reignite hostilities with Iran before the vote to change public opinion or disrupt the upcoming election. Difficult words: contend (to assert something strongly in an argument), adversary (an opponent or enemy in a conflict), reignite (to restart a conflict). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The ongoing war with Iran is the main topic in the upcomin g Israeli elections. Most Israeli voters want attacks against Iran to continue. Opposition parties strongly criticize Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for not winning. Opposition leaders warn that Iran still holds dangerous amounts of uranium which could quickly be turned into nuclear weapons. Other politicians propose bombing Iran’s energy facilities to destroy its economy and overthrow the government. Although politicians agree that Iran is an enemy, they fear Netanyahu may restart military strikes right before election day to get votes or delay the election process. They argue that winning the election is the priority , while future military steps should wait until a new leader is in place. Difficult words: upcoming (happening in the near future), overthrow (to remove a leader of government by force), priority (something more important than other things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Israel is getting ready for a big election . The conflict with Iran is an important topic . Many people want to keep fighting Iran. Opponents of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu say that he does not win the war. But he says that he will do it. Other politicians say that Iran still has nuclear materials. Israel is a dangerous country for them. Others want to bomb Iranian oil and energy sites to hurt its government. Some leaders also worry that Netanyahu may start new attacks just before the election. It can make more people vote for him. Difficult words: election (when people choose a leader), topic (what you speak or think about), opponent (a person who has different ideas than the leader). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A judge in Kenya has begun delivering a verdict in a landmark mass murder trial involving doomsday preacher Paul Mackenzie and 29 of his followers. The group faces charges over the deaths of 191 people, almost all of whom were children. Mackenzie established a remote camp in a forest, where he convinced hundreds of devotees that the end of the world was approaching. He instructed his followers to starve themselves to death so they could meet Jesus faster. He ordered that children be starved first, followed by women, and finally men. Police later uncovered hundreds of decomposed bodies in shallow mass graves scattered throughout the forest. Despite the horrific allegations and extensive physical evidence, Mackenzie and his co-defendants have pleaded not guilty, and claimed that no one was forced to die. Grieving families who lost entire households are waiting for the court’s verdict, and they hope it will finally bring closure. Difficult words: preacher (a person who gives religious speeches), devotee (a strong believer or follower), allegation (a statement claiming that someone has done something wrong or illegal, made without proof yet). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A court in Kenya is delivering a verdict in a mass murder case involving a cult leader named Paul Mackenzie. Mackenzie and 29 followers are accused of killing 191 people, mostly young children. The man led hundreds of people into a forest in southern Kenya. He convinced them that the world was ending and told them to stop eating so they could go to heaven. Police found many bodies buried in mass graves in the forest. Families who lost their children and loved ones are still deeply hurt by the tragedy. Mackenzie and his followers say they are not guilty and they didn’t force anyone to stop eating. Today, families are hoping the judge’s decision will bring them peace. Difficult words: mass murder (killing a large number of people at the same time or over a short period), cult (a religious group with extreme beliefs), mass grave (a single grave with many dead bodies). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A judge in Kenya is deciding a big case against a man named Paul Mackenzie. He is a cult leader. Officials say that Mackenzie and 29 people kill 191 people, mostly children. He takes his followers to a quiet forest. He tells them to stop eating so they can see Jesus. Many people starve and die. Police find their bodies in the ground. The man says that he does nothing wrong. He does not make anyone stop eating. Sad families are watching the court today. They want to get answers and live normal lives again. Difficult words: cult (a religious group with extreme ideas), follower (a person who likes the teachings or leading of someone), starve (to eat no food for a long time). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Thousands of visitors are expected to attend Belgium’s annual autumn pumpkin festival at the historic Groot-Bijgaarden castle near Brussels. Organizers anticipate around 50,000 people will visit the event, which celebrates the diverse and creative uses of squashes and pumpkins. The displays feature thousands of vegetables sourced from across Belgium as well as distant countries like Portugal and Germany, with sizes ranging from small varieties to a massive 772-kilogram giant. Despite a challenging growing season caused by a hot summer, the festival offers far more than just a harvest exhibition. Attendees can participate in pumpkin carving workshops ahead of Halloween and even watch some of the largest pumpkins being used as makeshift kayaks. The popular seasonal celebration successfully brings together families and gardening enthusiasts to enjoy autumn traditions and appreciate the remarkable versatility of this large vegetable. Difficult words: attendee (a person who officially attends or is present at an event, meeting, or festival), makeshift (serving as a temporary substitute for something else), versatility (being able to adapt to many different functions or activities). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A famous autumn pumpkin festival opened at a castle near Brussels. Around 50,000 visitors are expected to attend it. The event celebrates pumpkins and squashes of all shapes and sizes, brought from Belgium, Portugal, and Germany. The biggest pumpkin at the festival weighs an impressive 772 kilograms. Even though the summer was very hot and made farming difficult, the harvest display is still wonderful. Visitors can enjoy many fun activities, such as carving pumpkins for Halloween or watching giant pumpkins used as boats on the water. Families and autumn fans gather at the castle to celebrate the season, enjoy the festive atmosphere, and see creative pumpkin art. Difficult words: squash (a vegetable similar to pumpkins), impressive (something big, important, or of good quality), festive (cheerful and full of joy). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A big pumpkin festival is happening at a castle near Brussels, Belgium. About 50,000 people will visit. They will see many pumpkins and squashes . The pumpkins come from different countries and have many sizes. There is one huge pumpkin which weighs 772 kilos. Even though the summer is very hot this year, the festival is full of wonderful things. People can carve pumpkins for Halloween, look at big vegetables, and even see pumpkins which look like small boats. Families love to go there to celebrate autumn and have a fun day out. Difficult words: squash (a vegetable similar to pumpkins), weigh (how heavy something is), huge (very big). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kenya’s Dandora is Nairobi’s main dumping ground and one of the world’s largest landfills. It’s filled with single-use plastics despite Kenya’s efforts to reduce its environmental impact. The country advocates for a binding international agreement on plastics as delegates gather to discuss the first-ever treaty on plastic pollution. In 2017, Kenya imposed stringent laws against plastic bags, risking imprisonment or hefty fines. The recent Waste Management law places responsibility on producers rather than consumers. Biof Foods, a Kenyan dairy company, adapted by replacing white PET milk bottles with clear ones, receiving positive feedback from recyclers. The shift in mindset, influenced by recent legislation, reflects a growing environmental consciousness among Kenyans. Difficult words: binding (obligatory), stringent (strict or extremely limiting), consciousness (awareness). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Kenya’s Dandora landfill in Nairobi is one of the world’s largest landfills. The site is full of single-use plastics, although the country is trying hard to be more eco-friendly. Kenya wants a global deal on plastics, and delegates are meeting to discuss the first deal on plastic pollution. In 2017, Kenya implemented strict laws against plastic bags, with severe penalties for their use. The recent law makes producers responsible for plastic waste, rather than consumers. A Kenyan dairy company responded to the new law by switching to clear PET milk bottles. Many people welcomed this because it became easier to recycle milk bottles. This shows that Kenyans are changing their mindset and they want to deal with the problem of plastic pollution. Difficult words: single-use (a thing which people use only once and throw away), penalty (something you have to do or pay if you break a law or rule), mindset (a person’s way of thinking and opinions). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kenya’s biggest landfill is called Dandora. It is in Nairobi. It is one of the biggest landfills in the world. Dandora is full of throwaway plastics. People use most of these plastics only once. Then they throw it away. Kenya is trying hard to be cleaner. Kenya wants a strict global rule on plastics. Countries are talking about it now. In 2017, Kenya makes tough laws about plastic bags. People can go to jail or pay a lot of money if they use plastic bags. Now, a new law says that companies must handle their products’ waste , not consumers . A Kenyan milk company changes its bottles to clear ones. It is easier to recycle these bottles. People like this change. It shows that Kenyans care more about this problem than before. Difficult words: landfill (a place where people put things which they do not need anymore, and it looks like a mountain), waste (things which people and companies throw away), consumer (a person who buys things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Ideas of a space elevator have been around since the 19 th century; however, we still continue to rely on tried and tested methods of getting into space. Rockets use a lot of fuel to get into space, and they have to carry fuel to lift the fuel, therefore, getting to the Moon or Mars costs millions of dollars. With a space elevator, the cost could be reduced to dollars per kilogram. The basic idea of a space elevator is a cable that’s pulled thanks to a counterweight . The elevator stays vertical because the counterweight is thrown outward by the Earth’s rotation and the base is held down by gravity. Early ideas suggested building a cable from Earth up into space; however, the materials needed to withstand such enormous weight don’t exist. Physicists have come up with a solution, carbon nanotubes , a supermaterial stronger than other materials. But there are estimated millions of objects orbiting the Earth, and they could cause significant damage to the elevator. Difficult words: counterweight (a weight that’s as heavy as something else, so that the two objects can balance), withstand (to resist), nanotube (a material that has a tube-like structure and it’s composed of a large number of carbon atoms). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Since the 19 th century, scientists were thinking of building a space elevator. Getting into space is not cheap at all, because rockets have to carry a lot of fuel to be even able to leave the Earth. Therefore, getting to the Moon or Mars costs millions of dollars. A space elevator would make getting into space much cheaper. The problem is that people don’t have the right technologies and materials to build such an elevator. Experts came up with the idea of using carbon nanotubes . This material is stronger than any other material, but even if it was possible to build the elevator, small objects which orbit the Earth would probably damage it. Difficult words: technology (machines, devices, and ways of doing things), nanotube (many carbon atoms together which look like tubes), orbit (to move around an object). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People use rockets to get into space. It is not cheap. The rockets are heavy. They need a lot of fuel to lift off. It costs millions of dollars to get to the Moon or Mars. For a long time, scientists are thinking about a space elevator. The elevator uses the Earth’s gravity . But people don’t have the right materials and technologies to build it. No material is strong enough. One idea is to use carbon nanotubes. This material looks like tubes. It is many carbon atoms together. Carbon nanotubes are stronger than other materials. But there is a problem. Millions of objects fly in the atmosphere. Even if people build the elevator, these objects will probably damage it. Difficult words: fuel (materials which people burn and they produce heat or power), gravity (the force which pulls things towards the Earth), technology (machines, devices, and ways of doing things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bangladesh is currently facing the world’s worst measles outbreak. 200,000 suspected cases and more than 1,140 deaths have been reported since mid-March 2026. Most of the victims are young children under five. The crisis began after political protests in 2025 ended decades of leadership, which caused strikes, delayed vaccine orders, and a drop in national immunization coverage below the required 95% threshold for herd immunity . Although the government launched a massive emergency vaccination campaign reaching millions of children, internal documents show the response was hampered by weak data, rushed preparation, and severe rural gaps that missed millions of vulnerable youngsters. In remote regions, many grieving parents reported that health workers arrived too late. Experts warn that the outbreak serves as a critical global lesson on the dangers of declining vaccination rates, and urge nations to maintain strong routine healthcare systems to protect children from preventable diseases. Difficult words: immunization coverage (the percentage of a population that has received a specific vaccine to protect against a disease), herd immunity (indirect protection from an infectious disease when a large enough percentage of a population has become immune), hamper (to make an action or process difficult or slow down progress). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Bangladesh is struggling with a measles outbreak which caused thousands of hospitalizations and over 1,100 deaths, mostly among young children. The crisis started after political protests in 2025 disrupted routine healthcare and vaccination programs. Because fewer children received their shots, national immunity fell below safe levels. The government quickly organized an emergency vaccination campaign, but it missed millions of children due to bad planning, missing data, and a lack of outreach in rural villages. Many parents reported that health workers never visited their homes before their children fell sick. Experts say this health emergency is a strong warning to other countries about the importance of keeping vaccination rates high. Without strong immunization programs, preventable diseases can quickly return and kill thousands of people. Difficult words: measles (a dangerous disease which causes a fever and a red rash on the skin), hospitalization (taking someone to a hospital), outreach (providing services or medical help directly to people in local communities), preventable (able to be stopped before it happens). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Bangladesh is fighting a very bad measles outbreak . More than 200,000 people get sick, and over 1,100 people die, mostly young children. The trouble starts after political protests in 2025. They stop many children from getting their normal vaccines. Because of this, the country loses its level of protection . The government tries to solve the problem with a big emergency program. But many poor villages do not get vaccines. The planning is bad. Parents say that medical workers come too late to save their children. Experts say that this sad situation is an important message for all countries. It is important to keep their children vaccinated. If not, a disease can start very quickly. Difficult words: measles (a dangerous disease which causes a fever and a red rash on the skin), outbreak (a quick start or big increase in the number of sick people), protection (when people are safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The traditional tech market bargain where every new gadget offered better performance and storage for a similar price is under pressure due to the global AI boom . As tech companies rush to build massive data centers, they require huge quantities of specialized memory chips. Because chipmakers make much higher profits supplying data centers, consumer electronics manufacturers are facing a severe memory shortage and skyrocketing component costs. To cope, brands are raising prices, cutting down on device memory, or lowering specifications, which means consumers now pay more for devices with fewer features and slower speeds. Building new semiconductor factories takes years and billions of dollars, and chipmakers are cautious about overinvesting due to historic market crashes. As a result, experts predict high prices and minor upgrades will continue for the next few years. Consumers are adapting by keeping their phones and laptops for much longer or turning to the fast-growing market for cheaper, refurbished devices. Difficult words: boom (a sudden period of rapid economic growth, activity, or popularity), skyrocketing (increasing very quickly and by a large amount in a short time), refurbished (cleaned, repaired, and tested to work like new before being sold again). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Buying a new phone or laptop used to mean getting more memory and better speed for your money. Now, that is changing because of the huge demand for AI. Companies building AI data centers need a lot of memory chips. Chipmakers prefer selling to these data centers because they make much more money. This leaves fewer chips for everyday gadgets like phones and laptops, and causes component prices to rise sharply. To keep prices from doubling, manufacturers are selling devices with less memory and lower specifications . Because new phones cost more and offer fewer improvements, people are changing their habits . Many users are keeping their old devices for longer or buying cheaper phones instead of upgrading to the newest models. Experts say this situation will likely continue for the next few years. Difficult words: demand (the total amount of goods and services people are willing and able to buy), specification (a detailed description of the design and measurements of a product or machine), habit (what you regularly do). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

New phones and computers now cost more money. But they do not give you much better features . This is happening because companies building AI computers need a lot of memory chips . Chip makers prefer to sell to these big AI companies because they pay more. Because memory is hard to find, phone and laptop makers must raise prices or use less memory in their devices . People are not happy to pay more for less. Instead of buying new phones every year, many people now keep their old phones longer or buy used phones to save money. Difficult words: feature (a specific function of a product), memory chip (a small electronic part which stores information and runs programs), device (a piece of equipment or hardware, like a phone or computer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite its cold climate, limited farmland, and remote location, Iceland is using its natural resources, including geothermal heat, pure water, and clean renewable electricity, to transform food production. Innovators are building indoor and underground farms to grow crops that are usually difficult to cultivate in the North. For example, a former IT worker set up an underground farm growing thousands of sweet Japanese strawberries, which they sell locally. Other startups are finding clever ways to repurpose waste heat from data centers by channeling it into modified shipping containers to grow microgreens and fresh produce, which helps reduce the country’s heavy reliance on imported food. Additionally, advanced aquaculture facilities cultivate large amounts of microalgae in 10,000-liter reactors. They produce valuable natural compounds for dietary supplements and prove that the island’s unique environment offers a sustainable advantage for agricultural innovation. Difficult words: geothermal (relating to or produced by the natural heat inside the earth), cultivate (to grow and care for plants or crops under controlled conditions), microgreens (very small vegetable greens harvested soon after the first leaves appear, valued for intense flavor and nutrients). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Iceland has cold weather and very little farmland, but it has plenty of clean energy, hot water, and natural heat. Because of this, clever innovators are finding new ways to grow food indoors. For example, a former tech worker opened an underground farm where thousands of sweet Japanese strawberries grow successfully. Other startups are using waste heat from computer data centers inside shipping containers to grow fresh greens, which helps Iceland import less food from abroad. Near geothermal plants , companies are also growing microalgae in huge tanks. They use Iceland’s natural cold air to keep the tanks cool and clean geothermal energy to run the facility. These algae are then dried and used to make healthy dietary supplements. All these examples show how Iceland turns its harsh climate into a great advantage. Difficult words: innovator (a person who introduces new methods, ideas, or products), shipping container (a large metal box used to transport goods on ships, trucks, and trains), geothermal plant (a facility which uses heat from inside the earth to make electricity or provide heating). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Iceland is a cold island with very little land for farming. But the country has a lot of clean electricity, pure water, and natural heat. People are using these things to grow food in new ways. One man builds an underground farm to grow sweet strawberries. Other workers use warm air from data centers to grow fresh greens in small containers. Near power stations , a company grows small green plants in big tanks. It uses cold outside air and green energy. They turn these plants into healthy food supplements . These smart ideas help Iceland grow more of its own food. Difficult words: pure (clean), power station (a factory which makes electricity), supplement (a product which you take and it gives you extra nutrients in your diet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In a new global retirement index, Uruguay ranked as the best place in the world to retire abroad, and took the top spot from Portugal. The study compared 46 retirement and passive-income programs across several areas, including quality of life, travel freedom, citizenship routes, taxation , and costs. While Uruguay leads overall due to balanced scores, Europe remains the most represented region. Six spots are in the top ten, including Spain, Portugal, Latvia, Andorra, Italy, and Greece. European nations excel in living standards, strong passports, and safety, but often lose points for higher taxes and complex rules. For example, Spain ranks high for quality of life but lowest for taxes, while Portugal slipped to fifth place after increasing its citizenship requirement to ten years. Meanwhile, other regions offer different perks , such as tax benefits in Mauritius and the Middle East, or great affordability and fast citizenship across the Americas. Difficult words: taxation (the system of collecting taxes from citizens and businesses by the government), excel (to be extremely good at something or perform much better than others), perk (an extra advantage or benefit given in addition to regular pay or status). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A new study names Uruguay as the best country in the world for retirement , while Portugal drops to fifth place. The index looked at 46 retirement programs around the world. It checked quality of life, travel freedom, taxes, and costs. Even though Uruguay is number one, Europe still has six countries in the top ten, including Spain, Greece, and Italy. European countries are great for high living standards and safe travel, but they often have high taxes. For example, Spain is wonderful for living but has the highest taxes on the list. Portugal is still popular and affordable , but now requires ten years to get citizenship . Other parts of the world, like the Americas and Mauritius, are attractive because they offer lower taxes and cheaper living costs. Difficult words: retirement (the period of life after you stop working), index (a system which compares data), affordable (when people have enough money to buy something), citizenship (the legal status that you are a member of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A new report says that Uruguay is now the best place in the world to retire . Last year, Portugal is number one, but now it is fifth. The report looks at many countries to find the best countries for older people. Europe still has six countries in the top ten list, including Spain, Italy, and Greece. European places are very nice, safe, and clean, but they often have high taxes . Other parts of the world, like South America, have lower costs and easier rules. People who want to move abroad can choose what they like most, like good weather, low taxes, or easy travel. Difficult words: retire (to stop working, usually when you are older), tax (money you must pay to the government), abroad (in or to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Major supermarket chains across France were hit by an unprecedented cyberattack that targeted commercial refrigeration systems. Hackers remotely took control of thermostats in hundreds of stores, and raised temperatures in fridges and freezers to as high as 50°C. The sudden heat caused thousands of tons of fresh and frozen food, including meat, dairy, and juice, to spoil completely. This resulted in millions of dollars in damages and even triggered fires at several locations. The attack exploited security vulnerabilities in outdated control software, which allowed store managers to control appliances remotely. Major retailers like Intermarché and Carrefour were heavily affected, and forced some locations to manually disconnect their refrigeration units to prevent further tampering . French authorities and national cybersecurity agencies have launched an urgent criminal investigation into the incident, and raised serious concerns about the safety and security of essential infrastructure. Difficult words: unprecedented (an illegal attempt to damage, or steal data from computer systems or networks), thermostat (a device that automatically controls temperature in an appliance or building), vulnerability (a weakness in a system or software), tamper (to change something in order to cause damage or gain an advantage). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Big supermarkets in France suffered a strange cyberattack when hackers took control of their refrigerators and freezers. The hackers remotely raised the temperatures inside the appliances, which ruined huge amounts of fresh food like meat and dairy, and even started small fires in some stores. Big retail companies were badly hit, and lost millions of euros. Experts say the hackers broke into old software, which stores use to manage their fridges from afar. Because the software was outdated , the system was not secure. Store managers turned off remote controls to keep their shops safe. French authorities are investigating the attack to find out who is responsible. They also worry that more similar attack may come in the future. Difficult words: remotely (from a distance), outdated (old, not modern), investigate (to examine a crime or problem to discover the truth). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hackers attack big supermarkets in France. They use computers to make store fridges very hot. Because of the heat , a lot of meat, milk, and food goes bad. Workers must throw it away. Some stores are even on fire. The hackers break into an old software system. This system controls the fridges. Many stores lose a lot of money. They must turn off their machines to be safe. The French government is now looking for the people who do this bad thing. People are worried. They see that computer systems can be easy to break. Difficult words: fridge (a large appliance which keeps food fresh and cold), heat (when something is hot), turn off (to stop a machine or light). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
